* After several days of violence and confusion in [[Mauritania]], Pro-Israeli President [[Maaouiya Ould Taya]] appears to have defeated the [[2003 Mauritanian coup attempt|uprising against him]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/africa/2974006.stm |title=Africa &#124; Mauritania 'foils' coup attempt |publisher=BBC News |date=2003-06-09 |accessdate=2015-12-22}}</ref>
* The [[2003 Polish European Union membership referendum|Polish referendum on EU]] enlargement entrance finishes today; 78% of the voters voted to join the EU, with approximately 59% turnout.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/2973738.stm |title=Europe &#124; Poland says big Yes to EU |publisher=BBC News |date=2003-06-09 |accessdate=2015-12-22}}</ref>
* The presence of the [[monkeypox]] [[Virus (biology)|virus]] in the United States is confirmed with four cases in [[Wisconsin]], sparking the first discovery of the virus in the [[Western Hemisphere]]. Dozens of suspected cases have appeared across three [[Midwest]] states, where pet enthusiasts came into contact with infected domestic [[prairie dog]]s, which caught the disease from the [[The Gambia|Gambian]] giant [[rat]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Altman |first1=Lawrence K. |last2=Wilgoren |first2=Jodi |title=20 Cases of Disease Related to Smallpox Found in the U.S. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/06/08/national/20-cases-of-disease-related-to-smallpox-found-in-the-us.html |publisher=The New York Times |access-date=2022-05-24 |date=2003-06-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Four monkeypox cases confirmed in Wisconsin |url=https://www.cnn.com/2003/HEALTH/06/09/monkeypox/ |website=CNN |access-date=2022-05-24 |date=2003-06-09}}</ref>
